stages.do: Write the client's goal at the top of your page so every later answer can link back to it. If something isn't clear, interrupt politely and ask.
stages.say: "Sorry, before you go on: when you say X, do you mean…?"
stages.mistake: Faking understanding, then getting lost 10 minutes later.

stages.do: Recap the client, the problem and the measurable goal. Key points only, then check you have it right.
stages.say: "So our client is X, facing Y, and success means Z by [date]. Is that right?"
stages.mistake: Reading the whole prompt back word for word.

stages.do: Only ask questions whose answers would change your structure: how the client makes money, the target and timeline, scope, whether the whole industry is affected.
stages.say: "Is this a problem the whole industry has, or just our client?"
stages.mistake: Asking a list of questions to buy time.

stages.do: Ask for a moment. Draw 3-4 buckets, MECE, with second-level drivers specific to this case. Present it top-down, numbering the buckets.
stages.say: "There are three areas I want to look at. First… I believe the second is most likely the issue, so I'd start there."
stages.mistake: Generic buckets with no hypothesis, then asking 'where should I start?'

stages.do: After the structure, and after every answer, say where you want to go next and what data you need.
stages.say: "Next, I'd like to check whether the decline is industry-wide. Do we have market data?"
stages.mistake: Waiting for the interviewer to steer you.

stages.do: Ask for 30 seconds. Read title, axes, units and FOOTNOTE. Write down 2 insights and the so-what. Do the maths without being asked.
stages.say: "Two things stand out. First… Given our goal, the second matters more. Let me size it."
stages.mistake: Describing the chart instead of drawing insight from it.

stages.do: Say your approach before you calculate. Keep talking while you work. Sanity-check the size of every result, and round sensibly.
stages.say: "My approach is market × share × margin, minus the investment. Does that make sense before I run it?"
stages.mistake: Calculating in silence; dropping a zero.

stages.do: Even here, use 2-3 buckets (internal / external, short / long term). Add a real-world example. Keep one idea back for the follow-up.
stages.say: "Let me think about this in two buckets: what we can do with today's capabilities, and what needs new ones."

stages.do: Take 20 seconds to prepare, then speak for about 60. Recommendation, then 2-3 reasons with numbers, then risks, then next steps. Don't replay the case.
stages.say: "I recommend entering via a JV, for two reasons… The key risk is… so as next steps I would…"
stages.mistake: Opening with 'So, first we looked at…'

stages.do: Smile, especially when you're struggling. A pause comes across as composure; filler words come across as panic. Link everything back to the goal.
stages.say: "…and this matters because our client's goal is X."

sprints.how: 2-minute timer, draw a full structure, compare it to a model answer. Use the prompts in the Casebook.

frameworks.ask: Is the whole industry hit, or just us?
frameworks.build: Revenue (volume × price, by segment) · Costs (fixed vs variable, benchmarked) · Market (competitors, regulation, tech)
frameworks.trap: Diagnosing before splitting revenue by product / region / channel.

frameworks.ask: Which stream, segment or region is falling?
frameworks.build: Isolate the stream → customers × basket → market / customers / company / competitors

frameworks.ask: What is the goal, and over what time frame?
frameworks.build: Market attractiveness · Can we win? · Economics (investment, breakeven) · Risks · Entry mode (build / partner / buy)
frameworks.trap: Forgetting entry mode and timing; no pilot.

frameworks.ask: Growth from where: revenue split by business unit?
frameworks.build: Organic: existing customers, new segments, products, regions, channels · Inorganic: M&A, partnerships
frameworks.trap: A list of ideas with no sizing or priority.

frameworks.ask: Why does the client want to buy?
frameworks.build: Target on its own (market, profit, quality) · Synergies (revenue + cost) · Risks & fit · Deal (price vs value, build vs buy)
frameworks.trap: Ignoring integration risk and the do-nothing option.

frameworks.ask: What return does the fund need, and over how long?
frameworks.build: Market · Target vs peers · How we add value · Exit (buyers, multiple, timing) · Returns maths

frameworks.ask: What is the product worth to the customer?
frameworks.build: Cost-based floor · Competitor reference · Value-based ceiling → strategy (penetration vs skimming)
frameworks.trap: Using only one lens; no volume assumption.

frameworks.ask: How big is the threat in revenue terms?
frameworks.build: Understand the threat · Options: do nothing / mitigate / copy / partner or buy · Choose on impact, cost, speed, risk

frameworks.ask: Is demand real, and can existing capacity be squeezed?
frameworks.build: Demand · Industry supply (price effect) · Economics (breakeven, payback) · Alternatives (outsource, lease) · Execution

frameworks.ask: Goal: lower cost, more capacity, or reliability?
frameworks.build: Map the process & cost base → biggest driver first → people / process / technology levers → benchmark

frameworks.ask: Units or value? Which geography? Any limiting factor?
frameworks.build: Hypothesis first → top-down or bottom-up → segment → round numbers → sanity-check the other way

frameworks.ask: Valuing a standalone business or a stream of cash flows?
frameworks.build: DCF · Trading comparables (P/E, EV/EBITDA) · Transaction comparables; use at least two
frameworks.trap: Adding up future years without discounting.

frameworks.ask: What does success look like for citizens and for the budget?
frameworks.build: Stakeholders & objectives · Current performance vs benchmark · Levers (policy, delivery, funding) · Implementation & risks
frameworks.trap: Forcing a profit lens onto a social goal.

frameworks.ask: Who is it for, and what does success mean?
frameworks.build: Clarify → goal → users (both sides of a platform) → pain points → solutions → prioritise → MVP → metrics
frameworks.trap: Only looking at one side of a two-sided platform.

frameworks.ask: Improve on which measure (engagement, revenue, UX)?
frameworks.build: Mission → pick a user and use case → journey friction → solutions → impact × effort → metrics with guardrails
frameworks.trap: Defaulting to the biggest user group.

frameworks.ask: How is it measured, since when, sudden or gradual?
frameworks.build: External (season, competitors) vs internal (releases, bugs) → segment the drop → hypothesise → test

formulas.note: Revenue = volume × price; costs = fixed + variable
Margin is always on revenue
Markup is on cost. Don't mix it up with margin
Drives all breakeven maths

formulas.formula: Fixed costs ÷ Contribution margin per unit
formulas.note: 'How many units to justify it?'
Compare with the client's time frame
Compare with the hurdle rate
Before interest, tax, depreciation & amortisation; base for multiples
Launch and bid decisions
Quick NPV of a steady stream
i.e. return > cost of capital
Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ growth %
Say whether it is units or value

formulas.formula: % change in volume ÷ % change in price
formulas.note: State the volume assumption behind any price move
Check before adding capacity

formulas.formula: Profit per customer per year × years retained
formulas.note: Compare with CAC; healthy LTV:CAC ≈ 3+
Payback under ~12-18 months is healthy
Retention = 1 - churn; avg lifetime ≈ 1 ÷ churn

formulas.formula: Each cost line ÷ Revenue, over time
formulas.note: Finds the cost that is ballooning
A cash trap in growth cases

skills.name: MIND · Dual n-back
skills.how: Any dual n-back app. Start at 2-back; move up only above 80% accuracy.
skills.trains: Holding the structure, numbers and goal in your head at once.

skills.name: MIND · 60-second recap
skills.how: Play 2 minutes of a business podcast, pause, recap it aloud in 60 seconds: 'three things were said…'
skills.trains: Summing up under time pressure, which is the core of chart insights and recommendations.

skills.name: MIND · Structure recall
skills.how: Read one row of the Frameworks tab, close it, redraw it from memory, check the gaps.

skills.name: MIND · Speed maths
skills.how: Speed-maths app: percentages, big multiplications, breakevens. Accuracy first, then speed.
skills.trains: Faster arithmetic leaves more attention for thinking.

skills.name: VOICE · Articulation
skills.how: 2-3 tongue twisters: slow and exaggerated, then at speed.
skills.trains: Crisp diction. Mumbling is the first thing interviewers notice.

skills.name: VOICE · Paced reading
skills.how: Read a business article aloud, slightly slower than feels natural, honouring every full stop.
skills.trains: Controlling your pace. Measured speakers sound senior.

skills.name: VOICE · Pause practice
skills.how: Record a 2-minute answer. Count the ums. Re-record with a silent pause where each filler was.

skills.name: VOICE · Explain to the CEO
skills.how: Explain any formula or framework aloud in 60 seconds to an imaginary busy executive.

skills.name: FLUENCY · Read & listen
skills.how: 15 min of a strategy book, business press or a CEO interview. Note one story and one phrase.
skills.trains: Business vocabulary and real examples to use in cases.

skills.name: CALM · Breathe
skills.how: 10 min breath-focused practice daily; box breathing 4-4-4-4 before every mock and interview.
skills.trains: A calmer baseline and faster recovery when a case goes wrong.

fitQuestions.why: Can you structure your own story? 60-90 sec: arc → proof points → why here, why now.
Have you done real homework: people you spoke to, practice areas? Specifics, not brochure lines.

fitQuestions.q: A time you led through difficulty
fitQuestions.why: LEADERSHIP: do people follow you when it's hard?
Honesty and growth: a real failure, your share of it, what changed afterwards.
PERSUASION: show you understood the other side's position.
IMPACT: a quantified change that wouldn't have happened without you.
INITIATIVE: you started something nobody asked for.
A real one, and how you actively manage it.
